content:
jamie: quick sync: saw rehydrate storms after a batch demote -> eviction window yesterday. small tenants that were demoted then immediately evicted caused a flood of backend reads and prefetch retries.

anika: yeah saw that in telemetry. prefix_rehydrate_latency jumped and rehydrate_worker_queue length doubled. link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-prefix/rehydrate?from=now-1h

liam: root cause brainstorming: when we hard-evict, we remove residency meta. concurrent requests that race with eviction try to rehydrate; each one triggers an async-prefetch which then retries on miss. without a coordinated soft-state, we end up with N prefetches.

david: two orthogonal problems: (1) eviction lifecycle/visibility (how reads observe transitions) and (2) admission control for rehydrate workers. We should address both.

maria: proposal A (interface-first): define a read contract for prefix-state transitions. Readers see one of: HOT, DEMOTED, SOFT_EVICT, EVICTED. If SOFT_EVICT, read path must try to serve from small cache or enqueue a single rehydrate per prefix (dedupe). If EVICTED, fail-fast to backend.

liam: proposal B (lease-anchoring): when we demote, attach a short-lived lease token to prefix (lease ttl = hysteresis_ms). Readers that find no residency check if token exists and join/await the lease-holder rehydrate rather than issuing their own. lease-holder does single rehydrate and publishes result.

anika: leases sound elegant but we must handle leader loss and long tail if holder crashes. need TTL and fallback to force-rehydrate by others after expiry. also need to think about cross-shard reads where lease holder is on different shard. we want prefer-local-holder for perf.

jamie: tradeoffs matrix we discussed:
- Soft-state w/ dedupe: low complexity, uses extra memory, requires a per-prefix inflight set (or bloom-based dedupe).
- Lease token: fewer rehydrates, more complexity + failure modes, requires cross-shard RPC for handoff.

liam: implementation sketch for soft-state dedupe: keep small struct {state, last_access_ts, small_k_cache_ptr, inflight_rehydrate_id}. read path: if state==SOFT_EVICT and inflight_rehydrate_id!=0 then attach callback to that rehydrate future. otherwise CAS to set inflight id and start rehydrate.

code:```
# simplified state transitions
HOT -> DEMOTED on demote
DEMOTED -> SOFT_EVICT on demote_finalize (keep header+small-k)
SOFT_EVICT -> EVICTED on sweep or forced_eviction
```

and pseudo for read-path:
```
state = load(prefix.state)
if state==HOT: serve
elif state==SOFT_EVICT:
  if prefix.inflight_rehydrate_id != 0:
    await join(prefix.inflight_rehydrate_id)
  else:
    id = alloc_rehydrate_id()
    if CAS(prefix.inflight_rehydrate_id, 0, id):
      start_rehydrate(id)
      await completion
    else:
      await join(prefix.inflight_rehydrate_id)
```

anika: important: rehydrate dedupe must be bounded (joiners shouldn't wait forever). add per-wait timeout and fallback to cheaper model variant. also instrument stale_read_count and rehydrate_join_wait_ms histogram.

david: also watch correctness properties: read-after-write (RAW) for recent writes. If a writer committed to backend but prefix was demoted, we must ensure readers either see latest write or read from backend with linearizable semantics. That implies rehydrate must fetch latest sequence number and we should compare request.seq against prefix.last_seq. If request.seq > prefix.last_seq, route to backend.

maria: good call. we need a small on-disk pointer in soft-state: last_seq, maybe small tombstone map. Rehydrate should be able to return both payload and last_seq.

ops-bot: alert: rehydrate_worker_queue_depth > 128 in pool-staging for 3min :warning:

jamie: operational plan: implement soft-state + single-flight dedupe first (lower-risk). add a shard-local sweep that expires SOFT_EVICT after hysteresis_ms. per-shard limits: max_soft_state_entries and max_soft_state_bytes. when limit exceeded, pick least-recently-accessed SOFT_EVICT and force-evict. emit metric soft_state_force_evictions.

liam: per-shard timer: instead of per-prefix timers, maintain a priority queue keyed by expiry_ts and a single sweep loop that pops expiries every N ms. avoids timer explosion.

anika: telemetry to add: prefix_rehydrate_attempts, rehydrate_dedupe_rate, rehydrate_fail_rate, rehydrate_p95_latency, soft_state_memory_bytes, soft_state_force_evictions. Also a new SLO: rehydrate_success_rate > 99% over 1h.

david: rollout/canary: feature flag gated. Canary plan: enable on small subset of staging shards (pool-dev-2) for 24h, then k=10% of staging traffic, monitor prefix_rehydrate_attempts, backend_read_rps, 95/99 latencies. Backout if backend_read_rps increases or rehydrate_fail_rate > 1% for 10m.

maria: compatibility: default behavior must be identical for Dedicated customers unless they opt-in. expose config knobs: hysteresis_ms, max_soft_state_bytes_per_shard, rehydrate_join_timeout_ms, allow_force_eviction. Default hysteresis_ms=3000, rehydrate_join_timeout_ms=200, max_soft_state_bytes_per_shard=32MB.

liam: next steps: i'll prototype single-flight dedupe + per-shard sweep loop. jamie please draft RFC with state-machine, configs, and metrics. anika/david/maria will review for RAW semantics and UX. ops-bot please set temporary alerts for rehydrate_worker_queue_depth and soft_state_memory_bytes.

ops-bot: created alert ticket #KV-REHYDRATE-1 for rehydrate_worker_queue_depth threshold.

jamie: thanks. aiming to open RFC by EOD. comments?

anika: add a note in RFC about interaction with compaction and tombstone GC; soft-state must survive short compaction windows or be rechecked.

jamie: good point. will include. closing thread.
